mcq.q: Six friends A, B, C, D, E and F sit in a row facing South. F is second to the right of C. A is not at either end. E is at one of the two ends. A is immediately to the left of E. D is not at either end. There is exactly one person between E and F. Who is at the extreme right end of the row?
mcq.explain: Draw 6 seats and place the definite clues first (ends, middle, "immediate" clues), then test the remaining possibilities. Only one arrangement satisfies every clue: E – A – F – D – C – B (listed from West to East; facing South, their right hand points West). Reading the question from this diagram gives E. Remember that left and right are taken from the persons' own point of view.

mcq.q: In a row of students facing North, Kiran is 23rd from the left end and 24th from the right end. How many students are in the row?
mcq.explain: Positions from both ends count Kiran twice. Total = (position from left) + (position from right) − 1 = 23 + 24 − 1 = 46. Adding without subtracting 1 gives 47, which double-counts Kiran.
mcq.topic: Types of arrangement and types of information
mcq.fast: Total = left rank + right rank − 1.
